newsitem.title: UK: Russia plans intense Euromkt participation-Dubinin.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans intense Euromkt participation-Dubinin.

text.p: Russia plans to continue to play an active role on the international bond market, central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Friday.

"We had a good start on the Eurobond market with two successful issues and we hope to improve our situation and to continue our participation of the market very intensely," Dubinin told a conference on central and eastern European capital markets.
In November 1996, the Ministry of Finance, acting on behalf of the Russian Federation, launched its first international bond since the 1917 revolution -- a $1 billion five-year offering.
In March it launched a 2.0 billion mark seven-year bond.
Russian officials have said the next bond will be denominated in dollars. Russia also plans to launch a rouble-denominated Eurobond next year.
Added to this, Dubinin said Russia would ease restrictions on foreigners investing in its government securities market, making it easier to repatriate profits.
"We will continue liberalisation of the domestic securities market," he said.
